quiz.q: What does this print?  def f(a, b=2): return a * b   then   print(f(3))
rationales: b takes its default 2 when the call gives no value, so the result is 3 * 2.
A parameter with a default may be left out of the call.

quiz.q: Given def g(a, *, b=2): return a + b, which call is valid?
rationales: A parameter after * is keyword-only, so 5 cannot be passed by position.
A positional argument may not follow a keyword argument.

quiz.q: What is the value of x after  def h(): print('hi')   x = h()?
options: The name x is not created
rationales: 'hi' is printed, not returned; the call itself has no return statement.
The assignment happens; the function simply returns None.

quiz.q: What does sys.getrecursionlimit() report in a default Python 3.14 session?
rationales: The interpreter caps nested calls and raises RecursionError beyond it.
The default is 1000, not 256.

quiz.q: A function assigns spam = 'local' anywhere in its body but prints spam before that line. What happens on the call?
rationales: Any assignment in the body makes the name local for the whole body, so the global one is never read.
Python does not create a name with the value None.

quiz.q: Which change lets a function rebind a module-level counter?
options: Write  global counter  at the top of the function
Write  nonlocal counter  at the top of a module-level function
Nothing; functions can always rebind globals
rationales: nonlocal refers to an enclosing function's variable, not a module-level one.
Without global, an assignment creates a local name.

quiz.q: What does this print?  try: print(42 / 0)   except ZeroDivisionError: print('no')   print('done')
rationales: The program continues after the try statement, so done is printed too.
The except clause runs when the error is raised.

options: except ValueError, TypeError:  is a syntax error
except ValueError, TypeError:  catches either type, without brackets when no as is used
except ValueError, TypeError:  catches ValueError and names it TypeError
rationales: PEP 758 allows the unbracketed form from 3.14.
That was a Python 2 reading; it is not what 3.14 does.

quiz.q: Which keyword makes a function stop and hand a value back to its caller?
rationales: def only starts the definition.
pass does nothing.

quiz.q: You have written def hello(): ... and call hello() three times. Where does execution go at each call?
options: Into the function body, then back to the line after the call
To the end of the program
Into the body once; later calls are skipped
rationales: A call returns to its caller when the body finishes.
The body runs again on every call.
